page_title: Findly — 從螢幕邊緣一鍵滑出的 macOS 檔案抽屜

sources.entry: Findly - Finder-style file drawer that slides in from any screen edge with a hotkey and slides away when you switch apps. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/rocavence/Findly-app) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Findly
summary.one_liner: Findly is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that slides a Finder-style file drawer in from any screen edge via a hotkey, and hides it when you switch apps.
use_cases: quickly grab or drop files without switching to Finder
keep a file shelf that appears from a screen edge
browse Finder-like folders while working in another app
drag files between apps through a temporary drawer
access iCloud, external drives and tags from a slide-out panel
summary.what_it_does: Findly runs in the macOS menu bar. Pressing Ctrl + ~ slides a Finder-style drawer out from whichever screen edge the mouse is on, and Ctrl + Option + arrow keys choose a specific edge. When you switch to another app, the drawer slides back off-screen, and pressing the hotkey again brings it back. The file list supports four-column sorting, grouping by kind, in-place folder expansion, and Finder shortcuts such as Return to rename, Cmd + Delete to trash, and Space for Quick Look. The sidebar mirrors Finder favorites and can include iCloud, external drives and tags. The author says it uses its own NSPanel window rather than controlling the real Finder, and that it needs no extra permissions beyond optional Full Disk Access.
notable: Summons from any screen edge with Ctrl + ~ and slides away when switching apps
Builds its own NSPanel instead of driving the real Finder via Accessibility
Mirrors Finder sidebar favorites, iCloud, external drives and tags
caveats: Not notarized by Apple; first launch needs a quarantine-removal terminal command or Homebrew install
Protected folders such as Desktop, Documents, Downloads and iCloud show empty without Full Disk Access
